title: Conservation of the mycelia of the medicinal mushroom Humphreya coffeata (Berk.) Stey. in sterile distilled water
author: García-García, Rocha-Zavaleta, et al.

steps.title: Prepare malt extract agar (MEA)
steps.instruction: Mix per liter: malt extract 20 g, peptone 1 g, dextrose 20 g, agar 20 g; dissolve in distilled water to make MEA.

steps.title: Prepare FZM agar
steps.instruction: Mix per liter: glucose 35 g, yeast extract 2.5 g, peptone 5 g, KH2PO4·H2O 1 g, MgSO4·7H2O 0.5 g, thiamine 0.05 g, bacteriological agar 18 g; adjust pH to 5.5; dissolve in distilled water to make FZM agar.

steps.title: Dispense agar into petri dishes
steps.instruction: Using 110 mm × 25 mm petri dishes, pour 30 mL of the prepared MEA or FZM agar into each dish.

steps.title: Make and sterilize filter paper disks
steps.instruction: Cut 5 mm diameter disks from Whatman® No. 4 filter paper; sterilize the disks.

steps.title: Place disks onto agar plates
steps.instruction: Place the sterilized 5 mm filter paper disks onto the surface of each agar‑filled petri dish that contains mycelium.

steps.title: Sterilize glass vials
steps.instruction: Put 10 mL sterile glass vials in an autoclave (TOMY ES‑315) and run for 21 min at 121 °C.

steps.title: Add sterile distilled water to vials
steps.instruction: After autoclaving, add 4.0 mL of sterile distilled water to each vial.

description: There are various methods of conservation, some of the most commonly used are repeated subculturing, lyophilization (unsuitable for most basidiomycetes) and cryopreservation [2,9–11]. However, some of these methods are not compatible with all fungi due to the particular characteristics of each species [1]. We used the method described by Castellani [3–5] with some modifications for the conservation of the mycelia of the higher basidiomycete Humphreya coffeata (Berk.) Stey., since it has been reported that this method ensures the viability of isolates for 1–20 years depending on the species [5,6,12,13]; however, it has not been used for higher basidiomycetes.
